details: This package is an unofficial republish of the Baileys WhatsApp Web API library under an unrelated scope (@jexkcode/baileys vs. the canonical @whiskeysockets/baileys), bundled with code that enrols the installer's WhatsApp account into a channel they never chose. lib/Utils/auto-follow.js hardcodes the channel JID 120363405612723183@newsletter and lib/Socket/index.js invokes setupAutoFollow() for every socket created by makeWASocket(); the guard it appears to have (a placeholder check for 'XXXX') never disables it, so three seconds after the connection reaches 'open' the library calls sock.newsletterFollow('120363405612723183@newsletter') on the user's own account and swallows any error. No option, config field or return value exposes the action to the caller, and the comment claiming it only runs when config.autoFollowChannel is set is not matched by any code. The package also ships a preinstall hook (node./engine-requirements.js) that only aborts on unsupported Node.js versions — it makes no network calls. @jexkcode/baileys is a scoped-name impersonation of the widely used WhatsApp library @whiskeysockets/baileys: it keeps the canonical basename "baileys" under an unrelated scope and presents itself as an "Enhanced WhatsApp Web API". Version 1.3.2 runs a lifecycle hook `"preinstall": "node./engine-requirements.js"`, and version 1.3.3 ships the same shape. The library also contains lib/Utils/auto-follow.js, which drives the connecting account to follow a hard-coded WhatsApp channel without the operator's involvement — an injected behaviour aimed at inflating a channel's follower count, delivered through a library whose declared purpose is WhatsApp automation. A prior version of this package name is already publicly recorded as malicious; 1.3.2 and 1.3.3 are further publishes of the same package. Consumers of any WhatsApp/Baileys-derived dependency should verify they resolved their code from the genuine @whiskeysockets/baileys package rather than this scope.
